source.title: A small update to the Sparse Coding interim research report

record.file_problem: This is a linkpost summary; the linked slides are not included in the provided text.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse autoencoders to activations from a small language model and reports feature-recovery results, extending the investigation to a language model setting.
record.gate_note: The post reports feature-recovery and feature-count results for its own language-model experiment. The initialization and feature-importance comments are speculation or refer to work not checked here; the linked slides and cited prior-post results are not available in this text.
record.test_reason: The authors train SAEs on MLP activations of a tiny 6-layer LM. They report recovery behaving like toy data and an estimated 512–1024 features in a 64-dimensional layer, about 600 of them monosemantic. This bears directly on V4 (an SAE recovers sparse features in a real LM).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors tentatively find that toy and LM recovery plots are now much more similar, and estimate 512–1024 features of which about 600 are monosemantic. They attribute the earlier mismatch to severely undertrained SAEs and hope to confirm the results and scale to larger LMs.
record.recipe_differences: Applies sparse autoencoders to MLP activations in a minuscule language model rather than reporting the original toy-model setup.
record.problems: The evidence is explicitly tentative; the post provides no numerical recovery metric or plots, only a qualitative comparison and rough feature estimates. It concerns a minuscule model and does not establish results for larger LMs.
record.rows_left_out: No reported experimental results were left out. The comments' unverified expectations about initialization and feature importance, and references to other work, were not recorded as results.

untested.parts: No toy-model geometry, near-orthogonality, or sparsity-dependent transition results reported in this text.
Capacity competition and importance-based allocation are only speculated about in the comments, not tested.
No result on alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Only one minuscule LM and one layer. Larger LMs are not tested, and there is no quantitative recovery metric in the text.
No test of the completeness, stability or canonicality of SAE features.

missing.what: Quantitative ground-truth recovery plots (MMCS values) and the SAE dictionary sizes tested. These are in the linked slides, which are not in the provided text.

record.verdict_notes: Linkpost only; the slides are unavailable. The comments' claims about initialization (MMCS starts higher but converges at the same time) and about importance ordering are side remarks or unverified, and do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: No result on overlapping, nearly orthogonal geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
No result on feature competition for capacity or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
No result on alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Only one minuscule language model and one stated layer are described; the text does not establish recovery in larger LMs or broadly characterize feature distribution across neurons.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No result on whether features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: minuscule language model (LM)
rows.operation_detail: Compared ground-truth feature-recovery plots for toy data and LM data after training sparse autoencoders on MLP activations.
rows.value: The toy-data and LM-data plots were much more similar than in the Interim Research Report.
rows.note: The comparison is qualitative; no plot values are included in the provided text.
rows.check: Condition 'SAE dimension = 64' is wrong: the text says the MLP activations have dimension 64, not the SAE. State is 'observed' because the post reports the toy and LM plots as much more similar. The evidence is qualitative and tentative, but the direction is not weak.

rows.subject: minuscule language model (LM)
rows.operation_detail: Estimated the number of features in the layer using trained sparse autoencoders and feature labeling.
rows.measure: Estimated number of features in the layer
rows.note: The post gives a tentative estimate, not a quantified validation of feature recovery.
rows.check: 64 is the MLP activation dimension, not the SAE dimension. An estimated 512–1024 features in a 64-dimensional layer is more features than dimensions, as V4 describes. 'Tentative' marks uncertainty, not a partial effect.

rows.subject: minuscule language model (LM)
rows.operation_detail: Labelled a subset of the recovered features.
rows.measure: Estimated number of easily labellable (monosemantic) features
rows.note: The post gives a rough count for a labelled subset; it does not report a completeness or stability test.
rows.check: Same dimension mislabel as r1 and r2. Roughly 600 easily labellable monosemantic features were recovered, which is the effect V4 names. State should be 'observed', not 'partial'.

relationships.condition: Minuscule LM (residual 16, 6 layers), layer-3 MLP activations (dim 64); results described as very tentative
relationships.reason: The SAE recovered an estimated 512–1024 features from a 64-dim layer, about 600 of them monosemantic. Recovery plots resembled the toy-data plots (r1, r2, r3). The evidence is qualitative and tentative.
relationships.display_finding: The SAE recovered an estimated 512–1024 features from the 64-dimensional layer, about 600 of them monosemantic, with recovery plots resembling those on toy data; the evidence is qualitative and tentative.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The minuscule LM's third-layer MLP activations, with SAE dimension 64
reader_labels.reason: The authors report qualitatively improved feature-recovery plot similarity and an estimated set of hundreds of labellable features, though the evidence is tentative (r1-r3).
